in_context.text: Paul has just called the desire to be a bishop, or overseer, a good work (3:1). This verse begins his list of what such a leader must be like, and the list continues through 3:7. A similar list for deacons follows in 3:8-13.

speaker.text: Paul the apostle, writing to his co-worker Timothy. Many critical scholars think a follower wrote in Paul's name, while others defend Paul's authorship.

audience.text: Timothy, whom Paul had left to lead the church at Ephesus.

affected.text: Men being considered for the office of overseer in the church, and the church they would care for.

what.text: The verse lists qualities an overseer must have. He must be above reproach, faithful in marriage, sober, self-controlled, orderly, welcoming to strangers, and able to teach. These are mostly marks of character, not of talent or status.

events.text: The verse describes no event. It gives standing instructions for choosing church leaders.

written.text: Traditional view: about AD 62-64, between Paul's two Roman imprisonments. Scholarly view: many critical scholars date it around AD 80-110.

where.text: The instructions are for the church in Ephesus, a wealthy port city and capital of the Roman province of Asia. Where Paul wrote from is not stated, though it may have been Macedonia.

purpose.text: Paul wanted Timothy to know how people ought to behave in the household of God, the church. Choosing leaders of proven character was part of that.

big_picture.text: The letter teaches that sound belief and godly living belong together. Leaders must show this in their own homes and in their reputation with outsiders.

for_readers.text: The verse shows that the church judges leaders mainly by character. Some of the same qualities, such as hospitality, are asked of all believers elsewhere.

christians_differ.text: Christians read "the husband of one wife" in different ways. The Greek is literally "a man of one woman," and 5:9 uses the mirror phrase for widows. Main views include ruling out polygamy, requiring present faithfulness in marriage, or barring men who have remarried. Traditions also differ on whether "bishop" here names a separate office or the same role as an elder.

why_it_matters.text: The word literally means a watcher or overseer, a guardian of others. In Paul's later letters it came to name the head of a church.
The word is stronger than similar terms. It means a man has a good reputation and truly deserves it.
Together with the words for man and woman, it forms the phrase "a man of one woman." How this phrase is understood shapes the debate over what the verse requires.
The KJV says "vigilant," but the word means sober or temperate. It first described drink not mixed with wine.
This is the one item in the list about skill rather than character. Other passages link it to holding and explaining sound teaching.

takeaway.text: This verse is part of a list for choosing church overseers. It puts proven character, faithful family life, self-control, hospitality, and the ability to teach at the center of leadership.

unsupported.reason: Renders 'the husband of one wife' as 'faithful in marriage', which is only one of several readings (the card itself notes polygamy and remarriage views). It presents one interpretation as the meaning.
The cited sources only define the word as 'apt at teaching'. They do not say it is the one item in the list about skill rather than character; that is the card's own judgment.
